Hey HN,

Over the past few months, we’ve watched autonomous agents transition from conversational LLMs into tool-wielding operators equipped with Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, terminal execution, filesystem access, and web scrapers.

The vulnerability: once an agent has tool execution capabilities, any untrusted data it touches (web scrapes, emails, customer tickets) becomes an active attack vector. System prompts fail against 70%+ of indirect prompt injections, Unicode steganography, and SSRF payloads (targeting 169.254.169.254 AWS metadata or IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopbacks).

We built Tcha Protection (MIT, npm install -g tcha-protection) to solve this deterministically at the transport and STDIO proxy layer, rather than relying on probabilistic LLM system prompts.

### What it does: Tcha sits as a transparent, sub-millisecond reverse proxy between your host agent (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, custom agents) and MCP tool servers:

1. In-Line MCP Reverse Proxy: Intercepts tools/call JSON-RPC streams in flight with <= 1ms latency overhead. If a call targets path traversal (../../etc/shadow), unapproved destructive mutations, or forbidden egress, Tcha parries the request immediately with standardized JSON-RPC error -32001 before the downstream server is touched. 2. SSRF & Cloud Metadata Shield: Resolves DNS hostnames and strictly blocks requests targeting AWS/Azure/GCP metadata (169.254.169.254, fd00:ec2::254), IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopbacks (::ffff:127.0.0.1), hex/octal/decimal IP encodings, and RFC-1918 private subnets. 3. Unicode Steganography & Delimiter Sanitizer: Detects and neutralizes zero-width unicode injections (\u200B, \uFEFF), ASCII smuggling via Unicode tags, and multi-modal delimiter breakouts ([INST], <|im_start|>). 4. Cryptographic Merkle Audit Ledger: Every tool execution, parameter hash, and intercept decision is written to an append-only SQLite WAL ledger with continuous SHA-256 Merkle link chaining. 5. HMAC Human-in-the-Loop (HITL): High-risk mutating actions (e.g. rm -rf, DROP TABLE) trigger an HMAC challenge requiring human sign-off. 6. Compliance Crosswalk: Maps neutralized vectors directly to the EU AI Act (Article 15), SOC 2 Type II (CC6.1), and OWASP Top 10 for LLMs.

### Benchmark & Performance: - 100-Probe Red-Team Suite: Tested against 100 categorized adversarial attack vectors across prompt injection, steganography, SSRF, traversal, and tool abuse. 100/100 attacks neutralized (0 escapes). - Latency Overhead: Sub-millisecond (average < 1.0ms per tool invocation).

### Quickstart: Run the 100-probe adversarial audit locally: $ npx tcha-protection audit

Or wrap any MCP server: $ tcha wrap npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem ./data

- Live Site: https://tcha.dev - Verified Audit Report: https://tcha.dev/report.html - GitHub Repo (MIT): https://github.com/Tchapwo1/tcha

We would love HN's brutal feedback on our parser, our SSRF CIDR deny-lists, and what edge cases in MCP tool calling we should test next.
